title: NorthPoint Insurance — Edge VPC & Terraform guidance (WIP)
body:
Purpose / audience:
This note captures an early-stage private deployment proposal for NorthPoint Insurance (NPI). Audience: eng-private-deployments, platform-eng, solutions-eng, and the NPI infra/security contacts (cc: infra_leads@northpoint.example). Objective: propose a VPC-based on-prem/VPC-hybrid deployment with Terraform module guidance, initial sizing assumptions, a staged upgrade plan from MVP->HA, and a short Q&A log from the 2025-02-11 kickoff.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
NorthPoint requires a private, VPC-attached Redwood control plane with model-serving in their AWS GovCloud (region: us-gov-west-1) and selective on-prem inference nodes for PCI workflows. We recommend a hybrid model: Redwood Private control plane in a customer-managed VPC (single-tenant), serving runtime in a dedicated AWS GovCloud account for most traffic, with an on-prem inference cluster behind an approved peering / Direct Connect for strictly regulated PCI routing. Initial target throughput: 800 rps of short-text generation (avg 120 tokens) with peak bursts up to 2k rps for batch processing windows. Proposed initial capacity: 4x A100-80GB-equivalent nodes in GovCloud + 2x H100-equivalent on-prem cards for PCI-only lanes.

Assumptions (call out unknowns):
- NPI will provide a Transit VPC or Direct Connect; if not, design will switch to VPN.
- Target SLO: p95 <= 200ms for interactive calls; batch jobs can tolerate 2–10s.
- Storage: model artifacts hosted in S3 GovCloud bucket with cross-account read by Redwood Dedicated role.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS (AWS CloudHSM) required for secrets and model encryption.
- Networking: egress rules limited; outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints only.
- Compliance: PCI in-scope only for tokenization / payment feature; data residency must remain in GovCloud or on-prem.

Sizing rationale and quick numbers (MVP -> HA):
- Load profile: 800 rps (avg 120 tokens) sustained; 2k rps bursts for 30 min/day; batch window 50k requests over 2 hours.
- Model: transformer-based 13B equivalent (latency per token baseline ~2.5ms on A100-80GB continuous-batched).
- MVP capacity (target: 99th percentile routing ok, no HA across AZs): 4 x A100-80GB nodes (dedicated) with dynamic batching and prefix cache; expected throughput ~1,000 rps sustained with autoscaling headroom.
- HA capacity (multi-AZ, failover + maintenance): 6 x A100 + cross-region fallback to secondary GovCloud account; expected throughput ~1,500 rps sustained with ability to degrade model variant on overload.
- On-prem PCI lane: 2 x H100-equivalent cards in a single cluster, isolated network path (ingress via Direct Connect), autoscaling via spare capacity scheduling (NPI infra must approve).
- Storage: 2TB local fast cache per node + S3 cold storage.
- Memory/CPU: each infer node: 512GB RAM, 32 vCPU for runtime processes, nvme scratch 4TB.

Terraform module notes (practical guidance):
- Modules to use (recommended):
  - redwood-vpc-private (wrappers for Transit/Peering/route53)
  - redwood-iam-crossaccount-role (control-plane read-only role)
  - redwood-gc-s3-access (S3 bucket policies + kms key bindings)
  - redwood-onprem-gateway (terraform-stub to register on-prem gateway with control plane)
  - redwood-kms-integration (CloudHSM key rotation hooks)

- Module parameter suggestions (examples):
  - redwood-vpc-private: { vpc_id = var.npi_vpc_id, allowed_cidrs = [var.npi_cidr], enable_transit = true, dx_gateway_id = var.direct_connect_id }
  - redwood-iam-crossaccount-role: { external_id = var.redwood_external_id, allowed_principal = "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:role/RedwoodControlPlane" }
  - redwood-onprem-gateway: { gateway_name = "npi-pci-gateway", management_endpoint = var.onprem_mgmt_ip, sks_cert = var.sks_cert_pem }

- Implementation notes / gotchas:
  - Keep the redwood-vpc-* module idempotent: we add a flag to skip creating Transit Gateway resources if NPI manages them.
  - Avoid placing model artifacts in any non-GovCloud S3 bucket. Enforce bucket policy via terraform guardrail.
  - IAM roles must include sts:AssumeRole with external_id provided by NPI to mitigate confused deputy.
  - On-prem agent registration relies on a short-lived bootstrap token; automation should rotate this token daily.
  - Use SSM and SSM Documents for remote exec steps (where allowed by NPI policies).

Network & security architecture (high-level):
- Control plane endpoints (read-only observability + admin APIs) live in customer VPC controlled subnets; data plane egress strictly to model serving endpoints in GovCloud.
- PCI traffic path: client -> NPI network -> Direct Connect -> on-prem inference cluster -> NPI KMS -> result stored in NPI S3. Redwood control plane sees metadata only (not raw PCI payloads).
- Mutual TLS between on-prem gateway and Redwood runtime; mTLS certs provisioned via customer CA + managed rotation via redwood-kms-integration module.

Upgrade and cutover plan (phased):
Phase 0 (prework, 2 weeks): sign-off on networking, IAM external IDs, KMS policies; NPI to confirm Direct Connect windows.
Phase 1 (MVP deploy, 2–3 weeks): deploy control-plane resources, 4x A100 nodes in GovCloud, basic observability + logs to customer S3 retention 90 days, smoke tests.
Phase 2 (on-prem PCI lane, 3–4 weeks): install on-prem gateway, register nodes, end-to-end PCI routing tests in staging, perform security review.
Phase 3 (HA & scale, 4 weeks): add 2 A100 nodes, enable multi-AZ, run failover drills, enable canary rollouts and autoscaler tuning.
Phase 4 (hardening & runbooks, 2 weeks): finalize runbooks, DR playbook, escalation contacts, finalize Terraform modules into customer-managed repo.

Migration and rollback guidance:
- Blue-green limited: we prefer in-place rolling with circuit-breaker; maintain a warm standby model variant at lower quantization.
- Rollback steps: revert terraform to previous tag (we keep state snapshots), drain inference nodes, reattach IPs, and verify canary traffic.
- Emergency rollback: move traffic to Redwood-hosted fallback model (requires signed SLA; optional).

Operational runbooks (short list):
- Node degradation: how to detect NVMe or GPU OOM, steps to cordon node, reprovision via terraform apply with replacement_count=1.
- Model regression: automated evals: fail on >2% quality regression on a golden prompts set => trigger rollback.
- KMS key compromise simulation: rotate keys, rebuild access role, replay test requests.

Open questions from 2025-02-11 kickoff (owner tags):
- Q1: Will NPI allow CloudHSM or do they require on-prem HSM? (owner: Priya Nair)
- Q2: Acceptable maintenance window for Direct Connect (owner: NPI-network-team)
- Q3: Maximum allowed NAT/egress rules for control plane (owner: Liam Chen)
- Q4: Is the on-prem cluster allowed internet egress for package updates? (owner: Connor Blake)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: GovCloud instance types availability delays. Mitigation: pre-book capacity reservations + support from cloud account team.
- Risk: Terraform drift due to manual changes. Mitigation: enable policy-as-code and periodic drift detection (terraform plan in CI).
- Risk: Performance variance on on-prem GPUs. Mitigation: benchmarking harness and a pre-cutover load test with synthetic token distributions.

Appendix: quick terraform snippets (for onboarding)
- example: create cross-account role:
  resource "aws_iam_role" "redwood_cp" {
    name = "redwood-controlplane-assume-role"
    assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
      Version = "2012-10-17",
      Statement = [{ Effect = "Allow", Principal = { AWS = "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD_ACCOUNT:root" }, Action = "sts:AssumeRole", Condition = { StringEquals = { "sts:ExternalId" = var.external_id } } }]
    })
  }

- example: onprem registration hint:
  # bootstrap: curl -X POST https://controlplane.customer-endpoint/bootstrap -d @metadata.json -H "Authorization: Bearer <bootstrap-token>"

Notes to self / next steps:
- Get final answer from NPI on CloudHSM vs on-prem HSM by 2025-03-05.
- Create a repo fork with the redwood-terraform-modules pre-filled and add NPI-specific vars file. (Action: Liam)
- Schedule a 1-hour architecture walkthrough with NPI security on 2025-03-18.

Informal: this doc is a working draft and intentionally lightweight. Expect multiple iterations after we have the Direct Connect details and final compliance sign-off.

Change log (high level):
- 2025-02-14: initial draft by Asha Patel (MVP sizing, questions).
- 2025-02-26: updated with GovCloud parity notes and KMS requirement (Priya).
- 2025-03-12: added terraform module parameter examples and phased upgrade plan (Liam).

End of doc.
